title: refactor-private-deploy-terraform-modules-gpu-iam-network-layout
author: Priya Narang
description:
Motivation: As part of hardening Private deployments for GPU-backed clusters we ran into recurring drift and state complexity across customer modules. This PR refactors the Terraform module layout for Private to: 1) split GPU node pool concerns into a dedicated module with predictable lifecycle and tainting rules; 2) centralize IAM role creation and least-privilege policies so role drift is minimized and audit keys are clear; 3) introduce an explicit networking submodule that consolidates VPC/subnet/state mapping and removes implicit side-effects from other modules; 4) unify remote state layout to simplify state moves across workspaces.

Summary of changes: Consolidated modules into three first-class modules under modules/private: modules/private/gpu_node_pool_v2, modules/private/iam_roles, modules/private/networking. Added a state layout recommendation (remote_state.tf) and migration helpers in scripts/terraform-state-migration/README.md. Reworked variable names to be more explicit (cluster_id -> private_cluster_id, node_pool_suffix -> instance_group_suffix). Added new outputs to allow safe cross-module references without data sources. Implemented pre-apply validation via a new terraform/validate.sh to run fmt/validate/graph and a plan guard in CI.

Design notes: GPU node pool module includes: configurable accelerator_type, accelerator_count, gpu_draining_hook (pre-stop), taint labels for scheduling, and lifecycle rules to create new node pools rather than in-place mutation when switching accelerators. IAM module uses JSON policy templates with explicit versions and attaches roles by tags to avoid implicit name collisions. Networking module separates shared VPC (shared across multiple private deployments) vs dedicated VPC (single-tenant), and produces stable subnet ids as outputs for downstream modules. The remote state layout moves from many per-resource state files to a per-environment state with namespaced key prefixes (e.g. state/private/us-west-2/<cluster>/terraform.tfstate) to reduce lock contention during parallel applies.

Migration and backward-compatibility: This change is a breaking migration for existing Private installs. To minimize customer disruption we provide scripted helpers: scripts/terraform-state-migration/move-state.sh which uses `terraform state mv` with an explicit mapping file scripts/terraform-state-migration/mapping.csv and dry-run flag. Migration steps (high level): 1) git checkout the branch; 2) run ./terraform/validate.sh; 3) run terraform init against the old workspace; 4) run scripts/terraform-state-migration/dry-run.sh to verify mapping; 5) run scripts/terraform-state-migration/move-state.sh --apply; 6) terraform plan/apply in new layout. The README contains exact commands and an example mapping. We tested migration locally and on a QA cluster.

Testing and CI: Added unit-style tests using terratest snippets under test/ that validate module schema and a small integration harness that runs a plan against a mocked provider. CI changes: terraform fmt/validate/plan must pass before merge. Initial pipeline failed due to missing provider pinning; I updated providers.tf to pin to tested versions (AWS provider 5.x or GCP equivalent depending on target) and re-ran. Final CI summary is green.

Security and audit: IAM policies were tightened (removed overly-broad S3 access in favor of specific read/write buckets; deprecated legacy cross-account assume roles). Added audit metadata tags on IAM roles for automated detection. The networking module ensures that default security groups are not used, and explicit egress/ingress rules are required by the module input.

Rollout plan: We merged behind a feature flag controlled by the installer (installer uses module_version = "v2" by default only for new clusters). Existing clusters are not automatically migrated; customers who opt into the v2 path will run the migration script. We coordinated with Solutions Eng to prepare runbooks for three customers for an initial pilot.

Release notes: "Terraform: refactor private deployment modules (gpu node pools, iam roles, networking), introduce remote state layout and migration helpers. Breaking change: state migration required for existing Private clusters. See scripts/terraform-state-migration/README.md for instructions."

Docs: Updated docs site snippets in docs/private/terraform.md and added a migration guide docs/private/migration.md. Also added a sample values file at examples/private/values-gpu-v2.tfvars.

Why this was done now: recurring incidents where changing accelerator type caused nodepool replacement and resource name collisions, and frequent terraform state conflicts during parallel applies. This refactor reduces blast radius and standardizes lifecycle handling for GPU node pools while improving security posture for IAM and network boundaries.

review_thread: Evan Chen: Great direction. A couple of concerns: 1) state move complexity for customers; 2) provider pinning - please pin fully to avoid drift. Could we add a dry-run for state moves?
Author (Priya Narang): Added a dry-run script and expanded the README with example commands. Provider pins added to providers.tf as requested.
Marco Reyes: IAM policies look tighter but please avoid depended-on implicit names. Use tags for role lookup instead of names if possible.
Author (Priya Narang): Switched role lookup to tags and updated tests. Confirmed terratest covers lookup path.
Zoe Martinez: CI initially failed on fmt and provider versions. Verified final pipeline green and small nit about variable naming consistency (cluster_id -> private_cluster_id).
Author (Priya Narang): Renamed variables and left deprecation comments for compatibility for one release cycle. Added migration notes in docs.
Zoe Martinez: Approved and squashed commit suggestion accepted.
testing_notes: Unit-style terratest checks run in CI. Performed a full plan against QA account with a cloned state to validate state-move mappings. Performed GPU taint/replace test on QA cluster to confirm tainting + drain hooks work as expected. Manual validation was done by Solutions Eng in a staging tenant before merge.
release_notes:
- Refactor: private terraform modules (GPU node pool v2, IAM roles, networking)
- Add: state migration helpers and recommended remote state layout
- Add: CI validation and terratest checks
- Breaking: existing Private clusters require a manual state migration to adopt v2 modules; follow migration guide
notes_for_oncall: If customers report terraform plan failures after the installer upgrade, verify they have run the state migration helper. Common failure modes: missing mapping.csv entries or provider version mismatch. Check logs from scripts/terraform-state-migration/*.log in customer run; escalate to Infra if state move conflicts occur.
postmerge_tasks: 1) publish docs/manuals to docs site; 2) cut a release tag for terraform module v2; 3) notify Solutions Eng and SRE on the migration schedule; 4) monitor for state-move related incidents for two weeks
